result.note: Tests the August 2026 lifting of India's wheat export ban: the record harvest behind it and the global price context.

questions.prompt: In August 2026, India lifted its years-long ban on wheat exports. Consider the following statements about this decision:
items: It followed a record wheat harvest of 120.6 million tonnes.
It came when disruption in the Black Sea region had pushed global wheat prices to a two-year low.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because Black Sea disruption had pushed wheat prices to a two-year high, not a low. The move earns India diplomatic credit, but a future heatwave could force it to reverse course.
questions.source: India lifted its years-long ban on wheat exports after a record 120.6 million tonne harvest
